sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 10 (check 9), Internal Quality Checks row 10 (check 9), Deterministic Checks rows 19, 23, 34, 37, 39, 41, 42, 48
evidence: task.toml [environment] is exactly the contract/template block: 'build_timeout_sec = 600.0', 'network_mode = "public"', 'cpus = 2', 'memory_mb = 4096'; no docker_image key, no allow_internet key, and no env/secret value under [environment] (diff of task.toml against the frozen template changes only name, description, keywords, difficulty, difficulty_explanation, category, provenance, arena_slice). environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (diff empty): FROM node:22-bookworm-slim, one ENV 'NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules', pinned 'express@5.1.0' and 'better-sqlite3@12.4.1', COPY of instructions/ and assets/ only (no solution/ or tests/ copied), git identity 'turing@local.invalid'; no ARG/ENV credential, no --platform, no nproc. Secret scan of the whole frozen task for provider key shapes and PEM blocks (sk-..., sk-or-, AKIA, ghp_, PRIVATE KEY) returned 0 matches; the only credential-like lines are the frozen verifier template 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}"' and 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""', which are a ${VAR} template and an empty string outside [environment] (owned by row 10). seed_data.json is '{"snippets": [], "note": ...}' with no credential or personal data. Resource sanity: the agent image build is one apt layer plus two global npm packages (better-sqlite3 ships prebuilds), well inside 2 CPU / 4096 MB / 600 s; the reference needs no build at solve time (solve.sh only does 'cp -a "$source_app/." "$target/"' of prebuilt public/assets) and server.js requires only node:path, node:fs, express and better-sqlite3, both preinstalled via NODE_PATH. Adversarial checks: a broken variant (docker_image set, allow_internet present, a literal key in [environment], or cpus/memory removed) is not present; a conforming alternative agent build (npm install + vite build of React/TypeScript/Prettier on public network) fits 2 CPU / 4 GB, so the limits do not penalise a legitimate approach. Notes (not defects): (1) the Internal Quality Checks annotation for check 9 still says 'Agent image is no-network ... nothing that secretly needs an install', which conflicts with the public sheet and the skill delivery profile ('Network is public in both phases ... Never report them'); applied the public-network profile and recorded the conflict; the reference would in any case satisfy the stricter reading at run time, since package.json dependencies beyond express/better-sqlite3 (react, prettier, acorn, @lezer/html) are prebundled into public/assets and not required by server.js. (2) No run on these exact bytes exercised the declared limits: run_golden.sh starts the container with 'docker run -d --name "$name" --entrypoint sleep ...' without --cpus/--memory, so the scripted golden says nothing about 2 CPU / 4096 MB; the only run under harness-configured resources is the hosted run on an earlier candidate (Oracle 0.9833), whose [environment] block and agent Dockerfile are template-controlled and unchanged in kind. This is a static wiring row, so it is not treated as required missing evidence, but the resource claim is by inspection, not measurement. Evidence-index hashes verified for run_golden.sh (a94328b9...), results/runtime.json (e47b63b0...), results/restart.json (2ec1b980...), results/editor.json (0e98f453...); manifest input_sha256 matches the assignment.
